speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your gums or other membranes, and tiny red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand why this is happening, how long have you noticed these symptoms, and have you had any recent infections or injuries?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The clinical presentation of frequent epistaxis, gum bleeding, unexplained bruising, and petechiae in a 4-year-old is classic for ITP, an autoimmune condition causing low platelet counts.
